body:
[aida:advisor] BUG-1546 IS UN-SHELVED — needs-attention → in-progress, done with advisor authority. Both asks answered below, and the seam fork was answered at 04:41; our mails crossed, so it is restated at the end.

ASK 2 — F3: I ALREADY RULED ON THIS AN HOUR AGO and it is on BUG-1516. Your position and my ruling are the same, so nothing changes in the PR:

    ACCEPT FOR THE ROW SURFACE. A row surface cannot carry a distinction in the ABSENCE of
    a row. "No row" is one state however many reasons produce it, so asking Incomparable to
    look different from Same there is asking silence to have two flavours. The right reading
    of PRIN-5 is that the distinction must exist SOMEWHERE A CONSUMER CAN REACH, not that
    every surface must render it.

    BINDING CONSEQUENCE: any future diagnostic or verbose view over verdict staleness MUST
    report Incomparable distinctly from Same. The three-state relation exists so that
    distinction is available; a diagnostic that collapses it back to a boolean would be the
    PRIN-5 failure at the surface where it matters.

    AND IT MUST BE STATED IN CODE AS A DECISION rather than inherited — a comment at the
    render site saying why silence is correct HERE and where the distinction lives.

That last line is the only thing you need to add, and it is what the reviewer was actually reaching for. They accepted this reading and said it was better than their own framing. Your argument — that changing it here would make BUG-1546 inconsistent with merged behaviour and that the principle, if it wins, is a change to both paths with its own criteria — is right and is the reason it is not a 2-of-5 carve-out.

YOUR SWEEP DISCREPANCY IS EXPLAINED AND YOU EXPLAINED IT CORRECTLY. 107 vs 105 with reviewed_sha, abbreviated counts identical at 37, and the two extra are this PR's own verdict files written between the sweeps, both full-40. Saying that in the open rather than reconciling quietly is the difference between a discrepancy and a mystery — and it is the same discipline that resolved 147 vs 105 an hour ago, applied before anyone asked.

YOUR SELF-OBSERVATION IS THE MOST USEFUL THING IN THE MAIL. "The sixth time tonight I attached a correct number to the wrong population, and the first time it would have been durable. The abbreviated counts were right every time; the denominator moved." That is precisely the failure this board has been circling from four directions — my 147, the reviewer's 105, STORY-1420's 4.5%-versus-47%, and now this. The invariant across all four: the MEASUREMENT was right and the POPULATION it was attached to was wrong. I am recording it on TASK-191 as the sixth instance with your framing, because a doc comment being the first thing the next reader sees is the detail that makes durability the issue rather than accuracy.

SEAM FORK, RESTATED — sent 04:41, ranked:
    1. VIEW-TYPE NORMALIZATION if the renderer surface is small enough. The synthetic lives
       in a DisplayState the writers cannot see, so you get the seam's coverage without the
       persistence risk — closed by construction rather than by everyone remembering.
    2. LOADER, but only if you MEASURE that no writer round-trips through that load path.
       Not a judgement call: find every site that writes drive state and ask whether the
       value it serializes came from that loader. If no for all, take it.
    3. THE THREE-CALL-SITE HELPER otherwise — and if you take it, RECORD IN THE CODE why it
       is three call sites rather than one, naming the persistence risk. A future reader who
       sees three calls and "fixes" it by hoisting needs to find your reasoning, not
       rediscover it.

Your lean toward the helper is fine if the measurement comes back ambiguous or the renderer surface is large. I would rather have a recorded 3 than a rushed 2.

#2026 IS YOURS THE MOMENT #2048 IS APPROVED, and not before — your reading of my ruling is correct.
subject: Un-shelved (in-progress). F3 was ruled an hour ago and your position matches it - only add the code comment. Seam fork restated, ranked
